nodes.title: H3 MOTION CONTEXT - QUICK START
widgets_values:
H3 MOTION CONTEXT - QUICK START

This workflow chains clips so motion AND audio continue across joins.

FIRST CLIP OF A CHAIN (nothing to continue from yet):
- Mute/bypass the H3 Motion Context group
- Generate as normal. Save Latent runs with clip_index = 1

EVERY CLIP AFTER THAT:
- Unmute everything
- Load Latent clip_index = the clip to CONTINUE FROM (previous clip)
- Save Latent clip_index = the clip you are making NOW
  (making clip 2 from clip 1: Load = 1, Save = 2)

The saved latent carries BOTH picture and sound, so you do not need to
load the previous clip's video from disk. Wire nothing into
context_frames.

DON'T LIKE THE RESULT? Just queue again. Change nothing.
The retry reloads the previous clip and overwrites its own reject.

When you LIKE it: bump both index numbers and go again
(Load 1, Save 2; Load 2, Save 3; and so on).

SETTINGS THAT WORK (tested):
context_length "22", audio_context_length 24.
Those are the only two settings on the node. Everything else that used
to be exposed had one right answer and is now fixed in code.

Concatenate the trimmed clips with a plain butt join - no crossfade
needed. Latents save to output/h3_context/
(clip_00001.safetensors = clip 1).

Dark Blue Headers: H3 Motion Context nodes
Green Headers: nodes that need a number changed between clips

IMPORTANT:
- Video context length is a dropdown: 5, 22, 39 or 56 frames. Those are
  the only lengths the model's video latent can represent exactly.
  Start at 22.
- Audio context length is any number of frames up to the full clip.
  Capture only as much as you need to carry the sound forward.
- The pinned frames come back at the START of the new clip and the Trim
  node removes them, so a chained clip is 22 frames (0.92s) shorter than
  it was generated. Any timing you write into the prompt lands against
  the longer version, so a beat written for 4.0s arrives at 3.08s in the
  file.
- Turn Spectrum off. Turbo LoRAs also cost you audio quality. If a chain
  sounds duller or closer than you expected, try those before blaming
  the chaining.

If you have rgthree installed, the Fast Group Bypasser node makes the
mute/unmute step one click.

nodes.title: User Prompt
widgets_values:
integrated_multimodal_description: 
Begin [Shot 1] with a continuous medium shot of a slender Caucasian 23-year-old young woman walk down the sidewalk in Las Vegas at dusk, tracked by the camera from the front while maintaining the center frame. The camera tracks her at a slow and steady pace, capturing her full figure as she walks, and dollies back to keep pace. As she walks, the camera remains focused on her, shifting its position slightly. The girl's features are visible in detail, with no additional props or distractions in the frame. 

overall_soundscape: 
The overall soundscape comprises the ambient noises of the Las Vegas strip at dusk.

non_diegetic_music: N/A

Vaporwave title sequence look: pink and blue gradient palette, VHS tracking artifacts, Greek statue motifs, chrome palm trees, RGB chromatic aberration, lo-fi retro atmosphere, mood languid and nostalgic.

Timeline:
[0s-1s] VHS static opens the frame, the title "COMFYUI" appears with RGB split and a slight horizontal jitter.
[1s-2.5s] Hard cut, a Greek plaster bust close-up, pink-purple gradient sky, a pixelated sun.
[2.5s-4s] Clean "STARRING" credits appear, "LATENT" and "CONTROLNET" each shown exactly once.
[4s-5s] Final card "DIRECTED BY COMFYUI" holds, one VHS tracking glitch settling into stability.

Hard cuts only, transitions landing with tape jumps, no push-ins, no dissolves.

Audio: lo-fi vaporwave score, slow drum machine with soft bass, VHS tape-noise sample joins at 2.5s, melody fading for the last 1s.

All text must be clearly legible, do not misspell English, no Chinese characters, do not repeat names or job titles, no soft dissolves, no subtitle bars.

nodes.title: H3 MOTION CONTEXT - QUICK START
widgets_values:
H3 MOTION CONTEXT + REFERENCE MODE - QUICK START

Same chaining as the T2V setup, with reference images, video or audio
steering the look. Your references are kept and the continuation audio
is added alongside them. Nothing to configure for that.

Needs H3 Motion Context from August 2026 or later. Older versions
refused to run reference mode and chaining together.

WIRING:
MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo -> H3 Motion Context -> guider / sampler
References go on the reference node as usual. Motion Context sits after
it and leaves them alone.

FIRST CLIP OF A CHAIN:
- Mute/bypass the H3 Motion Context group
- Generate as normal. Save Latent runs with clip_index = 1

EVERY CLIP AFTER THAT:
- Unmute everything
- Load Latent clip_index = the clip to CONTINUE FROM
- Save Latent clip_index = the clip you are making NOW
- Keep the same references wired as the previous clip

Retry and index handling are identical to the T2V note above.

SETTINGS THAT WORK (tested):
context_length "22", audio_context_length 24.

PROMPTING IS THE HARD PART HERE. Read this bit.

The pinned frames are not a suggestion. They are re-injected at every
sampling step and the model cannot render anything else in that span.
So if the prompt for clip 2 opens describing something different from
how clip 1 ended, the model does not choose between them - it renders
BOTH. Clip 1 ends on a close-up of one character, clip 2 opens asking
for a two-shot of two others, and you get three people in the frame.

The fix: open every prompt by describing how the PREVIOUS clip ended.
Same person, same clothes, same framing, same action. Let that run for
a beat past the join, then change to whatever you actually want. The
pinned frames get a stretch of timeline that agrees with them, and the
change happens where nothing is pinned.

Give the hold something to do - a breath, a weight shift, an eyeline
change. A held framing with nothing happening in it renders as a frozen
frame and looks like the video stalled.

At 22 frames of context the pin is 0.92s, and you want a beat past that,
so plan on the change landing around 1.5 to 2 seconds in. On a 5 second
clip that is most of the first half. Longer clips are easier than a
shorter hold.

REFERENCES HAVE NO TIMING. Every reference conditions the whole clip.
There is no way to say "this one applies from two seconds in." If the
outfit, location or character changes partway through, the shot
structure and the description have to carry that on their own.

Dark Blue Headers: H3 Motion Context nodes
Green Headers: nodes that need a user input between clips
